design:
Decided with the operator on 2026-10-29:
- **Scope is a third filter beside agent and search, not a replacement.** All three apply together.
- **The board remembers its scope** per project, in this window, as the board's column folds already are (`TasksScreen.tsx`, `FOLDS_KEY`) and as the spec page will remember its document. Not stored on the Hub. A remembered spec that no longer has tasks falls back to All.
- **A list of task ids stays a separate narrowing.** A coverage row or a loop link still narrows the board to exactly the tasks it names, which is often narrower than a spec (one requirement's tasks). While it is set it overrides the scope; clearing it returns to the scope, which it never changes.
- **A spec page opens the board on its spec.** Its existing "Show these on the board" (`SpecHealthLine.tsx:208`) sets the one-spec scope instead of a list of task ids, so the board then reads as that spec and keeps reading so.
- **One spec shows that spec's whole history.** The board's default hides completed tasks of archived specs (`exclude_archived_completed`); choosing an archived spec on purpose shows them.
- **What the board can show is not capped by the page it loads.** The board loads the oldest 1000 tasks (`PAGE_SIZE`, `api/tasks.ts:593`); a narrowed board must show every task in its scope even in a project past that.
- Not mocked first: the control is one picker in the existing filter row, in the existing chip style.

open_questions.question: Does the chosen scope stick? Answer: yes, per project in this window (operator, 2026-10-29).
Does a coverage row's or loop link's list of task ids become the spec scope? Answer: no, it stays a separate narrowing that overrides until cleared (operator, 2026-10-29).
Should a spec page link to its tasks on the board? Answer: yes; its existing 'Show these on the board' opens the board scoped to the spec (operator, 2026-10-29).

problem: The board shows every task of the project in one set of columns. The live project holds 101 tasks from 27 specs (84 from approved specs, 9 from archived ones, 8 with no spec; read from the :8000 database, 2026-10-29), so following one build means reading past every other spec's cards. The only narrowing today is by agent and by a text search on title or id (`BoardView.tsx:90-96`), plus a one-off list of task ids a coverage row, a loop link or a spec's "Show these on the board" sets (`activeTaskIds`, `App.tsx:539`, `:564`; `SpecHealthLine.tsx:208`), which says only "linked from the specification" and cannot be chosen from the board. Every task already records its spec (`spec_document_id`, null for a hand-made task), and the Hub's task list can already filter by one spec (`api/v1/tasks.py:983`), so the information is there and the board does not offer it.

requirements.rationale: 27 specs carry tasks in the live project; a list that cannot be narrowed by typing is a scroll hunt.
requirements.statement: The Tasks board offers a scope of All, No spec, or one spec. The spec choices are every spec in the project that has at least one task, each shown by title with its number of tasks, and the list narrows as the operator types part of a title.
With one spec chosen, the board shows exactly the tasks whose spec is that document, in every status, including the completed tasks of an archived spec, however many tasks the project holds.
With No spec chosen, the board shows exactly the tasks that belong to no spec, however many tasks the project holds.
With All chosen, the board shows the same tasks it shows today, including hiding the completed tasks of archived specs.
While the scope is not All, the board names it (the spec's title, or No spec) and how many tasks it holds, and offers one action that returns to All.

The scope, the agent filter and the search apply together: a task shows only if it is in the scope, matches the agent filter and matches the search. The agent filter's counts count only tasks in the scope.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-29: the board should remember my choice. Kept in the window, as the board's column folds are, not on the Hub.
requirements.statement: The board reopens in the scope the operator last chose in that project, in the same browser window profile, after leaving the Tasks tab, switching project and back, or reloading the app. Each project remembers its own scope. A remembered spec that no longer has any task opens as All.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-29: keep it separate. A coverage row names one requirement's tasks, narrower than a spec.
requirements.statement: A list of task ids sent to the board by a coverage row or a loop link narrows it to exactly those tasks while it is set, whatever the scope, and says so as it does today. Clearing it shows the board in the scope it was in before, and setting or clearing it never changes the remembered scope.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-29: a spec page should link to its board. The link already exists and sends a list of task ids; scoping instead makes the board read as the spec and keeps it so.
requirements.statement: A spec page's 'Show these on the board' opens the Tasks board scoped to that spec, and that scope becomes the remembered one.

On the trial Hub, in a browser, choosing a spec on the board shows exactly its tasks, choosing No spec shows exactly the unbound ones, All shows what the board showed before, the choice survives a reload, and a spec page's link opens the board on that spec.
